profile.reading:
Tahoe Reno 3 is one of the named future buildings on Switch's "Citadel Campus" in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County, Nevada, adjacent to the Tesla Gigafactory. Switch's only public reference specifically naming Tahoe Reno 3 is a November 19, 2020 press release describing site preparation as "beginning" on the building, one step earlier in the construction process than the "accelerated" construction language used for the neighboring Tahoe Reno 2 in that same release; no individual square footage, megawatt, or completion-date figures were given for either building, with the full future campus build-out described only in aggregate as "more than 7 million square feet and over 600 megawatts." Switch's FY2021 SEC 10-K filing, covering the period through December 31, 2021, lists the Citadel Campus portfolio as one current facility (Tahoe Reno 1) plus seven future facilities totaling 5.89 million gross square feet and 520 megawatts combined, without breaking that total out by individual building, meaning that as of Switch's last public-company financial disclosure, Tahoe Reno 3 had not yet opened and had no individually reported specifications. This OSM record shares the same 1 Superloop Circle address as Tahoe Reno 1 and the other numbered Tahoe Reno buildings in this dataset, consistent with all being part of one large campus rather than having individually distinct street addresses. Switch's current marketing describes the full Citadel Campus at up to 17.4 million square feet and more than 2 gigawatts of power at completion, a scale increase from the 2020-2021 figures reflecting continued campus expansion since Switch's December 2022 acquisition by DigitalBridge and IFM Investors.

Storey County's Tahoe Reno Industrial Center spans roughly 107,000 acres and hosts more than 100 tenants beyond Switch, including Tesla's Gigafactory and Google, drawing more than 900 megawatts of on-site power generation capacity across the broader industrial park. Switch's 2020 press release describing site preparation beginning on Tahoe Reno 3 specifically cited "multi-megawatt expansions with global e-commerce and semiconductor clients" as the demand driver behind the campus's continued build-out, tying this building's development timeline to named customer categories even though Switch has not disclosed which specific tenants occupy or are contracted for the building.

reading.body:
Tahoe Reno 3 is a future data center on Switch's Citadel Campus in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, adjacent to Tesla's Gigafactory. As of Switch's last public financial disclosure in its December 2021 10-K filing, Tahoe Reno 3 had not yet opened and no individual specifications had been published for it. Switch stated in November 2020 that site preparation was beginning on the building, one phase earlier in construction than the neighboring Tahoe Reno 2, and cited demand from global e-commerce and semiconductor clients as the driver for campus expansion, but disclosed no completion date or capacity allocation for this specific building.

The Citadel Campus as a whole has been described in progressively larger terms: as of 2021, Switch projected the full build-out at over 600 megawatts across more than 7 million square feet across multiple future buildings; by 2023, after acquisition by DigitalBridge and IFM Investors, marketing materials described the completed campus target as more than 2 gigawatts across up to 17.4 million square feet. The 2021 10-K reported seven unnamed future facilities totaling 520 megawatts and 5.89 million square feet in aggregate, without breaking those figures out by individual building. Tahoe Reno 3's share of that total cannot be determined from published sources.

In Nevada, Tahoe Reno 3 sits within a state where only 2 of 26 mapped data center facilities publish megawatt figures, totaling 10.37 MW reported statewide. The Citadel Campus as a whole ranks third by published capacity in Nevada, though individual facility figures are not public. The Tahoe Reno Industrial Center itself draws more than 900 megawatts of on-site power generation capacity across more than 100 tenants beyond Switch, making the broader site a major industrial power consumer in the region.
